item.title: The Promise And The Proof
item.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. item.title: Police arrest Abuja man over alleged rape, cyberbullying of women
item.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has arrested a man, identified as Usman Mohammed, over alleged rape, sexual assault, cyberbullying and intimidation of women under the pretext of recovering debts owed to him. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a statement, saying the suspect allegedly targeted women, including widows and other vulnerable persons, through predatory money-lending practices. Adeh said the suspect was arrested on Friday, November 6, 2026, following a report received at the Lugbe Police Station at about 7:05 p.m., alleging that he had been intimidating, sexually assaulting and physically assaulting several women over debts owed to him. She said operatives from the Lugbe Division, led by the Divisional Police Officer, immediately launched efforts to track down the suspect. According to her, the suspect was traced to the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Lugbe, where police operatives moved to arrest him. However, he allegedly attempted to escape upon sighting the officers by speeding off in his vehicle. The police said the operatives gave chase and eventually intercepted him before he could gain access to the expressway. Adeh said preliminary investigations identified Mohammed as a resident of FHA Lugbe, who allegedly used debt recovery as a pretext to intimidate and exploit his victims. She alleged that, in his latest incident, the suspect lured a woman into his vehicle and drove her to a secluded location in Lugbe, where he sexually assaulted and raped her. The suspect allegedly forced the victim to strip naked and recorded videos of her private parts, which he subsequently used to threaten to expose her publicly and kill her if she failed to meet his repayment demands. The police spokesperson said Mohammed was currently in custody and undergoing further interrogation. She added that he would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, condemned all forms of violence, sexual exploitation, intimidation and cyberbullying. He urged residents, particularly vulnerable persons, not to suffer in silence but to report cases of abuse, threats, blackmail and other criminal activities to the nearest police station. The Command also provided emergency contact numbers for members of the public: 08032003913 and 08061581938. item.title: CNG to save Kano tricycle riders ₦8,200 daily — MDGIF
item.description: Commercial tricycle operators in Kano State could save about ₦8,200 daily on fuel costs by switching from petrol to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), the Executive Director of the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), Oluwole Adama, has said. Adama disclosed this on Tuesday during the commissioning of two Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) facilities established by the MDGIF in partnership with Rolling Energy Limited in Kano. He explained that an operator who spends about ₦14,200 daily on 10 litres of petrol would spend approximately ₦6,000 on CNG for the equivalent energy, resulting in a daily saving of ₦8,200. According to him, the savings could amount to nearly ₦250,000 monthly, providing tricycle operators with additional income to meet household expenses, pay their children’s school fees and save towards owning their tricycles. “Here in Kano, a litre of petrol sells for about ₦1,420, while the same amount of energy from CNG costs about ₦600. That is less than half the price,” Adama said. The two facilities commissioned are the LCNG Mother Station at Tamburawa and a Daughter Station at Hotoro Quarters in Tarauni Local Government Area. Adama said the facilities could support the refuelling of up to 2,500 cars and tricycles daily, while also supplying gas to other refuelling stations. He added that they could serve up to 200 trucks daily, helping to reduce transportation costs and ease the movement of goods from Kano to other parts of the country. The MDGIF executive director disclosed that the Tamburawa Mother Station had the capacity to handle 300,000 standard cubic metres of gas daily. He urged fleet owners, transport unions, businesses and investors to take advantage of the facilities, while calling on Rolling Energy to maintain high safety standards and ensure reliable services. Earlier, the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Rolling Energy Limited, Mubarak Umar Danbatta, said the projects would bring gas supply closer to businesses and investors in Northern Nigeria. He explained that the development would reduce the cost and logistical challenges associated with transporting gas over long distances, making it easier for businesses to establish CNG stations and industries that depend on natural gas. Danbatta said his company previously travelled hundreds of kilometres from Abuja to source CNG from Ajaokuta and Obajana in Kogi State before transporting it to supply its stations. “What Rolling Energy and MDGIF are doing here in Kano is changing that model. We are bringing gas closer to the people,” he said. He disclosed that the Tamburawa facility had a designed gas-handling capacity of five million standard cubic feet daily, with two LNG storage tanks of 55 metric tonnes each, while the Hotoro station had a storage capacity of eight metric tonnes. item.title: Kidnappers: I’ll sign execution warrant even for my father – Okpebholo
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has vowed to sign the death warrants of convicted kidnappers, regardless of their relationship with him, declaring that he would personally supervise their execution. The governor said he would not spare anyone found guilty of kidnapping, even if the convict were his father or a close family member. Okpebholo spoke in a video shared by TheCable on Tuesday, amid efforts by his administration to enforce the state’s law prescribing the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. “I pray our brothers are not involved because I will sign it. Even if it is my father, I will sign it. The truth is this: we just have to get some bad elements out of the system for the system to stand. “Because somebody will die. But these people are the ones killing people. How many people have we killed?” he said. The governor defended the proposed executions by highlighting the trauma and physical injuries suffered by victims of kidnapping. He cited an incident involving a woman who was allegedly pushed during an abduction attempt, saying the fear and trauma she experienced could have resulted in her death. He also referred to an attack on the state’s Chief Judge, who he said sustained serious injuries, including the loss of the use of one hand, during an encounter with kidnappers. “Just look at the way they were pushing that woman down there. Supposing she died at that, because of fear, only fear. It’s enough for her to die. People have gone through trauma. “Even our Chief Judge, if you see our Chief Judge, one of his hands was cut off by kidnappers,” he added. Okpebholo said he had contacted the state Attorney-General to ascertain the status of the relevant documents and was awaiting further action. He, however, vowed to pursue the cases through the appeal process, insisting that convicted kidnappers would not be allowed to escape punishment. “But we still follow them up on the appeal. We won’t just let them go like that. So we will get to wherever they stop, we will take them from there. We will not spare anybody. “I stand, if I see this paper today, now, I will sign it and I will even supervise the killing,” he said. The governor’s comments come amid the implementation of the Edo State Kidnapping Prohibition (Amendment) Law, 2025, which introduced the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. The Edo State House of Assembly passed the amendment in February 2025, and Okpebholo signed it into law later that month. Under the amended law, kidnapping offences in which victims survive attract life imprisonment, while those directly involved in abductions resulting in the death of victims face capital punishment. The law also prescribes penalties for individuals who aid, abet or provide support for kidnapping activities. item.title: Although No New Case, Nigeria Is Still Not Ebola-Free, NCDC Warns
item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has called for continuous vigilance from the public as Nigeria expects clearance from the World Health Organization (WHO) on Ebola spread in the country. The NCDC Director-General, Dr Jide Idris, called for nationwide alert on Tuesday as he gave an update after the country confirmed an imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease in a traveller from Uganda recently. According to him, although there are no reported new cases in the country, it is not over, as there are still 28 contacts being monitored before the WHO can give Nigeria a clean bill of health on the Ebola virus. The development was after Idris, on Tuesday, noted that 34 of the 62 contacts identified in connection with the case had completed their individual 21-day monitoring period as of November 9, while the remaining 28 were still under follow-up. He said the agency was sustaining contact tracing, investigation of reported alerts, laboratory testing and surveillance at points of entry in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the FCT Administration, state authorities and development partners. Idris cautioned against interpreting the 21 days since the first case was confirmed as the monitoring period for all identified contacts, explaining that each person has a separate 21-day follow-up period. “It’s remaining 28, and not all of them will go at once. So, although they have done 21 days in exclusion, they are still there. “Because they have left the quarantine does not mean we are Ebola-free. We can only be declared Ebola-free after another 21 days again. And it is not by ourselves to declare ourselves Ebola-free. WHO must be involved. “So as at now, although we don’t have any new case, we still have to be vigilant. We are still not Ebola-free. “Our surveillance system and contact tracing is throughout Nigeria. Some people manage the airport, other people manage the land borders. And you will recollect that we had alerts from Adamawa State and Rivers State. I think the last one was in Borno state that came through the borders. They all turned negative”, he said. This combo photo shows NCDC officials on duty in Nigeria, and response team members helping to wear protective suits before burying a person suspected of having died from Ebola in Bunia, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, on May 25, 2026. (Channels TV/GLODY MURHABAZI / AFP) He also stressed that being identified as a contact does not mean that a person has contracted Ebola. The monitoring is intended to ensure that anyone who develops symptoms is identified early and receives an appropriate response. The NCDC urged healthcare workers in public and private facilities to remain vigilant, establish patients’ travel and exposure histories, observe infection prevention measures and promptly report suspected cases to public health authorities. item.title: Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity — UNHCR
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nearly 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape escalating violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has said. The UN refugee agency, in a briefing issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, warned that the influx was worsening an already difficult humanitarian situation in Niger, which hosts more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. According to the agency, approximately 327,500 Nigerians are already seeking refuge in Niger, while several hundred others have reportedly crossed into neighbouring Benin Republic because of deteriorating security conditions in northern Nigeria. UNHCR’s Director of External Relations, Dominique Hyde, said most of the newly arrived Nigerians had settled in the border regions of Diffa, in southeastern Niger, and Tahoua, in the western part of the country. The agency disclosed that about 1,200 Nigerians crossed into Diffa in October, while another 3,400 arrived in Tahoua during the same period. It added that more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, had arrived in Diffa since the beginning of the year. UNHCR expressed concern over the harsh living conditions confronting displaced families, many of whom are staying in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean drinking water, healthcare and other essential services. Some women, it said, were forced to walk several kilometres daily to fetch water for their families, while humanitarian organisations had reported rising cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections and poor sanitation among the new arrivals. The agency also raised concerns over the registration of displaced Nigerians, disclosing that only about five per cent of those who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered. It warned that the lack of proper documentation was making it difficult for thousands of refugees to access humanitarian assistance and essential public services. The humanitarian crisis, according to UNHCR, is further compounded by insecurity and climate-related challenges in Niger, particularly in Diffa, where more than 70 per cent of the country’s reported security incidents this year have occurred. Despite the growing pressure, the agency acknowledged the support of Niger’s authorities and host communities, including the provision of land for temporary shelters. However, it appealed for increased international assistance, seeking $11.4 million to expand its humanitarian response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin. The appeal includes $2 million for urgent interventions covering food, water, shelter, healthcare, refugee registration and protection. UNHCR warned that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families fleeing violence could be left without access to essential humanitarian assistance. item.title: NERC approves N30bn for free meters, targets May 2027
item.description: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved N30 billion for the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF), targeting the provision of free electricity meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerated metering of Band B customers. The Commission announced the approval in Order No. NERC/2026/121 on the operationalisation of Tranche C of the MAF, which took effect on November 2, 2026. Under the arrangement, the N30 billion will be allocated among the 11 electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. NERC said the third tranche was designed to accelerate efforts to close Nigeria’s metering gap, with equitable distribution of meters across states within the respective DisCo franchise areas. The Commission directed the DisCos to conduct transparent procurement processes involving eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stocks. It said maximum procurement prices had been set based on the median national MAP online bid prices recorded during the September 2026 bid cycle. The order provides for payment to selected meter providers in two stages: 70 per cent upon verification of meter stock delivery and the remaining 30 per cent after confirmation of complete installation. NERC emphasised that all meters supplied and installed under the MAF programme must be provided to customers free of charge. It also directed that each meter must prominently display the name of the relevant DisCo, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription, “NOT FOR SALE”. The Commission further stipulated that where a DisCo initiates the relocation of an existing customer’s connection point for revenue protection purposes, the cost must be borne by the distribution company. It warned that sanctions would apply where defaults by DisCos impede or delay meter installation. To ensure transparency and accountability, the order also establishes monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements for the Fund Manager, DisCos and participating meter providers. All supply and installation contracts under Tranche C are required to be filed with the Commission, while the installation of all meters under the tranche must be completed on or before May 31, 2027. NERC urged electricity distribution companies and other stakeholders to comply strictly with the order, describing the initiative as part of efforts to close the national metering gap, strengthen revenue assurance, improve service delivery and protect electricity consumers. item.title: Anambra to prioritise erosion control in environmentally responsible communities
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has resolved to prioritise communities that demonstrate environmental responsibility in its interventions to control erosion across the state. The decision was taken at the weekly State Executive Council (EXCO) meeting in Awka, where the government said communities engaging in practices that worsen erosion would no longer receive priority attention. The prohibited practices include sand excavation, indiscriminate felling of trees, deforestation, dumping of refuse in drainage channels and directing stormwater onto roads. The State Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, who disclosed this after the meeting, said perpetrators of such practices would also be prosecuted to serve as a deterrent to others. Anambra has more than 1,000 active erosion sites affecting communities across the state, with experts arguing that addressing the scale of the problem would require federal and international intervention. Also at the meeting, the EXCO directed that Ogbodi in Amichi community, Nnewi South Local Government Area, which was recently cut off by gully erosion, should be reconnected within two weeks through palliative measures. Mefor said the process of identifying a permanent solution to the erosion problem would commence immediately. The erosion had cut off Ogbodi residents from other parts of Amichi, disrupting access and movement within the community. Meanwhile, the State EXCO approved what it described as the “Soludozie Anambra Framework”, an organised and inclusive platform designed to promote development through the Public-Private-Community Partnership (PPCP) model. According to Mefor, the initiative is intended to provide a structured channel through which Anambra indigenes at home and in the diaspora, as well as other well-meaning individuals, can partner with the state government to drive development. He explained that under the framework, the government’s role would generally be limited to documentation, recognition and support where requested, while donors and partners would directly manage their funds and projects. Mefor said the initiative was aimed at positioning Anambra as a model of collective governance and inclusive development, while accelerating the state’s development. item.title: Keyamo Flags Off Kogi International Airport Construction
item.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo (SAN), on Tuesday joined the Governor of Kogi State, Ahmed Ododo, to officially flag off the construction of the Kogi International Airport at Zariagi, declaring that the landmark project will place the state on the global aviation map and open up new frontiers of economic opportunities. A statement by Tunde Moshood, Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, noted that Keyamo, who was accompanied by the NCAA’s Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Michael Achimugu, and other top aides, participated in the historic ceremony alongside the Governor, members of the State Executive Council, traditional rulers, other dignitaries and the immediate past Deputy Governor of Kogi State, Edward David Onoja. Keyamo Flags Off Kogi International Airport Construction on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Speaking at the event, Governor Ododo described the airport project as a strategic investment in the economic future of Kogi State, emphasising its potential to unlock the state’s enormous agricultural and solid mineral resources for local and international markets. The Governor noted that Kogi State possesses immense economic potential which, if properly harnessed, could position it as a major contributor to Nigeria’s export economy. He explained that the airport would provide a significant boost to the transportation of agricultural produce and mineral resources, attract investors, stimulate commercial activities and create employment opportunities for the people of the state. He further highlighted the airport’s capacity to facilitate the movement of people and goods, strengthen connectivity, attract new businesses and accelerate the development of supporting infrastructure across the state. In his remarks, Keyamo described the flag-off as a historic milestone whose significance would endure for generations. “What is happening here today, what the Governor has done today, will resonate many, many years, centuries after today, 500 years from today. Do you understand the significance of what is happening here today? Let me tell you the significance. Today, as from today, this village called Zariagi will be on the Global Aviation Map,” the Minister declared. He explained that every recognised airport around the world is identified through a global aviation coding system, noting that the establishment of the airport would give Zariagi international visibility within the aviation community through the relevant identification and coding processes of the International Air Transport Association (IATA). According to him, the project represents a significant step in putting Kogi State on the global aviation landscape and connecting it to the wider world. item.title: Big Names Missing As World Leaders Take Stage At COP31
item.description: World leaders will take the stage at COP31 in Turkey on Wednesday, but some prominent names are missing from this year’s annual UN climate summit even as global warming intensifies. The two-week conference kicked off earlier this week in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, with governments under pressure to tackle the climate crisis after a year of heatwaves in Europe, deadly floods in Nepal and major wildfires in Indonesia. Dozens of leaders will speak during the “high-level segment” taking place on Wednesday and Thursday, including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian. But observers have pointed to the absence of some big names, with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham the only leader from a G7 country scheduled to address the summit. While European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen is coming to Antalya, French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni are skipping the event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi are also absent from the most recent list. “It is a shame that some of the bigger European leaders aren’t coming. We need Europe to be showing up strongly at this COP,” Cosima Cassel, a climate diplomacy expert at think-tank E3G, told AFP. Wopke Hoekstra, the EU’s top climate official, said the absences were “not completely atypical” as leaders may have “practical” reasons for not being able to attend a summit. Climate activists sing during a demonstration organized by Climate Action Network (CAN) Europe at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. But he also told reporters in Brussels that “expectations are not necessarily high” for this climate conference. Iran’s Pezeshkian said he would use the event as an opportunity to express Tehran’s position on environmental destruction in war. “At this conference, we will speak about the actions of the United States and Israel in destroying the environment,” he said before departing for Turkey, according to Iranian state television. The French government said Macron would be absent because November 11 is World War I Armistice Day and the president will attend an EU summit in Ireland on Thursday. “If top leaders want influence over where the global (energy) transition is going, showing up is a pretty good place to start,” said Chiara Martinelli, director of Climate Action Network Europe. “I am afraid that Ursula von der Leyen will be lonely on the stage while the leaders of the biggest EU economies are a no-show,” Martinelli said. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 11, 2026
item.description: The US dollar is trading at approximately ₦1,350 per dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), while the naira exchanges at between ₦1,411 and ₦1,419 per dollar in the parallel market on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Available exchange rate reports indicate that the official market rate was around ₦1,350.36 per dollar on Tuesday, November 10, while parallel-market dealers quoted buying and selling rates of approximately ₦1,411 and ₦1,419, respectively. At the parallel market, also known as the black market, the exchange rate varies depending on the location and the Bureau De Change (BDC) operator. The latest reported parallel-market figures indicate that Nigerians selling $1 to currency dealers could receive approximately ₦1,411, while those purchasing $1 may pay about ₦1,419. At the official market, the NFEM rate remains the benchmark for foreign exchange transactions in Nigeria. The difference between the reported official rate of ₦1,350.36 and the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,419 is approximately ₦68.64 per dollar. The exchange rate may change during the day depending on dollar supply, demand and trading activities across the foreign exchange market. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed currency dealers before carrying out foreign exchange transactions. item.title: Market conditions: Dangote Cement rescinds plan to list shares on London Stock Exchange
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Cement Plc, has rescinded plan to list its shares on the London Stock Exchange, LSE following market conditions. The company disclosed this after its Board Meeting held on Tuesday. In a statement sent to the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX and signed by Edward Imoedemhe Company Secretary, stated: “ This is to inform the Exchange, investing public and all stakeholders that at the meeting of the Board of Directors of Dangote Cement PLC held today, 10 November 2026, the Board resolved that, in light of current market conditions and the company’s strategic priorities, the company announces that it and its selling shareholder, Dangote Industries Limited (DIL) will not proceed with the proposed secondary listing and offering on the London Stock Exchange at this time. “ The company’s ordinary shares remain listed on the NGX, and this decision does not in any way affect the company’s operations or business plans. “Dangote Cement PLC remains focused on delivering sustainable value to its shareholders and building on its strong market position.” It will be recalled that Dangote had disclosed plans to list the cement business on the London Stock Exchange in May, eight years after an earlier attempt in 2018 failed. He had told the Financial Times that the proposed dual listing would involve selling about 10 percent of Dangote Cement’s shares on the UK exchange. item.title: Duke seeks opposition’s unity
item.description: •Warns against repeating 2023 mistakes, 1966 crisis •PRP unveils manifesto, makes candidates sign accountability pact By Clifford Ndujihe & Luminous Jannamike PRESIDENTIAL candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, Mr Donald Duke, has urged opposition parties to unite ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that failure to learn from the mistakes of 2023 could have grave consequences for Nigeria’s democracy. Read Also: Donald Duke: From Cross River record to PRP’s 2027 presidential gamble Duke, who spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the unveiling of the party’s manifesto, A Compact for Nigeria’s Renewal, cautioned that opposition parties must rise above personal ambitions and differences to defend the country’s democratic foundations. He expressed doubts about the possibility of free and fair elections under the prevailing political circumstances, alleging that the President Bola Tinubu-led administration was deploying state institutions and other mechanisms to weaken opposition parties. “What should be clear to us all, the players and the electorate, is that we would be foolish to expect a free and fair electoral process, what some may term a level playing field. This will not happen, was never planned nor intended to happen,” he said. Warning against repeating the political miscalculations of 2023, the former Cross River State governor said: “We erred in 2023 and we are repeating the same in 2027. It is said, fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me. The shame will certainly be on us.” He called for strategic thinking and unconventional approaches by opposition forces to confront what he described as an unguarded political establishment. “David did not defeat Goliath in a wrestling bout, but by strategy and unconventional means,” he said. Duke alleged that opposition parties were being frustrated through restrictions on access to public venues, advertising opportunities, political intimidation and the use of state institutions. item.title: 2027 countdown: Obi pledges to unite Nigeria, tackle insecurity, poverty
item.description: • No Nigerian should remain in IDP camp if I become President • We’ll hunt down kidnappers, ensure safe return of displaced persons — Obi • Every voter must protect, monitor and ensure transmission of votes •Don’t allow politics to worsen insecurity, Gbong Gwom Jos warns By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has pledged to unite Nigeria, tackle insecurity and lift millions of citizens out of poverty if elected President in 2027. Read Also: Obi, who spoke at a town hall meeting with supporters in Jos, Plateau State, on Tuesday, said national unity, security, economic recovery and accountable leadership would be the priorities of his administration. “Our number one commitment is to unite the Federal Republic of Nigeria because today we have no unity. We are divided along tribal and religious lines. That should not be. We are Nigerians,” he said. The former Anambra State governor identified security as another major priority, promising to end the killings, kidnappings and displacement of citizens across the country. “Number two is to secure Nigeria. It is our duty to ensure that Nigerians live in safety, in a country where people are no longer killed daily. “I assure you that no mother will continue to cry over the loss of her children. No woman should experience the pain of losing her husband, and no father should suffer the agony of losing his wife,” he said. On internally displaced persons, IDPs, Obi declared that his administration would prioritise their safe return to their ancestral communities. “If any Nigerian remains in an Internally Displaced Persons camp, we have failed. Once one Nigerian is in an IDP camp, the entire Nigeria is in an IDP camp. People must return to their homes,” he said. He vowed that kidnappers and other criminal elements would face decisive action. “Nobody will kidnap two children and disappear into the bush. If you kidnap children and go into the bush, you will not be alone there. We will come after you,” he warned. Obi, who recalled visiting troubled communities in Bokkos, Barkin Ladi and Mangu local government areas of Plateau State, said the plight of victims of violence informed his presidential ambition. “If I have one person in an IDP camp, it means we are all in an IDP camp. I am competing because I want to know how we talk to that mother whose child was killed, that husband who lost a wife and that woman who lost a husband. Who is going to listen to their cries?” he asked. He said the town hall engagements were designed to make leadership demand-driven by allowing citizens to articulate their needs rather than merely listening to campaign promises. “When you want to serve, you must listen to the people. When we come for campaigns, we only talk and we don’t listen to the people. We have decided that leadership must be demand-driven,” he said. item.title: Leave politics to politicians, northern minorities tell clerics
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Northern Nigeria Minorities Group, NNMG, has cautioned religious leaders, particularly imams and pastors, against partisan political involvement and the use of churches and mosques as platforms for political mobilisation. The group, which represents more than 200 minority communities across Northern Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), urged religious leaders to distinguish their spiritual responsibilities from partisan political activities, warning that inflammatory political messages from religious platforms could heighten tensions and expose Nigerians to violence. Addressing journalists in Abuja yesterday, the Convener, Jacob Edi, also known as Kakaki Bassange, said religious leaders should focus on praying for the peace and unity of the country, while leaving partisan politics to politicians. He said: “Politics is for politicians, religion is for pastors and imams. They should pray for this nation. They should pray for the peace and unity of Nigeria. “When a pastor or an imam tells you about peace, he is not looking for your vote. He is not even looking for your money. This is his duty. This is his calling.” Edi said anyone interested in partisan politics should relinquish religious leadership and join a political party to pursue such ambitions. “If he wants to come into politics, he should remove the garment or remove the jalabia or whatever and go to any party,” he said. The group also cautioned opposition politicians against actions capable of destabilising the country, urging them to resolve political disagreements through constitutional and judicial processes. item.title: Where are the meters?
item.description: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved a N30 billion disbursement to electricity distribution companies (DisCos) for the procurement and installation of meters under the meter acquisition fund (MAF) tranche C scheme. According to Order No NERC/2026/121, issued on Monday, the fund targets the provision of free meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerating installations for Band B consumers. The commission had approved N21 billion for the first tranche and N28 billion for the second tranche of the initiative. In the order, NERC said the funding would be shared among the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. Daily Trust reports that since the introduction of reforms in the electricity sector under the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu administration, the federal government has granted approval for the procurement of N1.116trn worth of prepaid meters for distribution to consumers for free. The reform, which saw the removal of electricity subsidy for Band A electricity customers, was meant to provide free meters for customers under the band, with extension to others in Band B, C, D and E. But despite the approval and release of funds, the rollout of the meters has been slow. Though the government maintains that the country has 12,747,789 electricity customers with 8,045,565 customers metered and 4,704,224 unmetered, many Nigerians still pay for their meters to stop alleged extortion by electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) through estimated billing. To reduce reliance on estimated billing and improve electricity-sector revenue collection, the government introduced new schemes worth N1.11trn from 2024 to date. The distribution has largely focused on Band A customers, whom the former Minister of Power, Adebayo Adelabu, said made up 15 percent of electricity consumers. Daily Trust reports that the schemes the government introduced include the Distribution Sector Recovery Program (DISREP), Meters Acquisition Fund (MAF) and Presidential Metering Initiative (PMI). A breakdown of the money allocated to each scheme showed that DISREP allocated $250m (N337bn at N1348.10/dollar) for 3.2m meters, MAF got N79bn and PMI was allocated N700bn. While the DISREP and MAF are ongoing, PMI will start next year, but the funds have been released to the agency spearheading it. item.title: Nigeria’s private sector foreign debt rise 179.6% to $54.5bn — World Bank
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The World Bank said that the foreign debt of Nigerian companies rose by 179.6 per cent in seven years to $54.48 billion in 2025 from $19.49 billion in 2018. This implies that Nigerian businesses now owe foreign lenders almost three times what they owed in 2018. The World Bank disclosed this in its International Debt Report 2026 which stated that Nigeria’s private sector nonguaranteed external debt stood at $54.476 billion as of December 2025. The World Bank explained that the total external debt of a country is the sum of public and publicly guaranteed debt, private nonguaranteed debt, and short-term debt. According to the World Bank, private sector nonguaranteed external debt refers to money borrowed by private companies from foreign banks, investors and other lenders without the government or any public institution guaranteeing repayment. “Private nonguaranteed debt comprises long-term external obligations of private debtors that are not guaranteed by a public entity. “Public and publicly guaranteed external debt comprises long-term external obligations (maturities of over one year) of all public debtors, including debt held by the central government and by state-owned enterprises. Short-term debt is defined as debt with an original maturity of one year or less ,” the report said. The 179.6 per cent growth in Nigeria’s private sector in the seven years was faster than the increase in government-backed external debt, which rose by 155.5 per cent from $24.422 billion in 2018 to $62.4 billion in 2025. The World Bank report showed that private companies’ foreign debt is becoming an increasingly important part of Nigeria’s external debt burden. In 2018, private sector nonguaranteed debt was equivalent to about 79.8 per cent of public and publicly guaranteed external debt. By 2025, it had increased to 87.3 per cent. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s total external debt, covering government borrowing, private companies’ foreign loans and short-term obligations, increased from $46.238 billion in 2018 to $145.015 billion in 2025. The report also highlighted the high cost of borrowing from private foreign lenders. According to the World Bank, new loans obtained by Nigeria from private foreign creditors in 2025 attracted an average interest rate of 9.6 per cent, compared with 1.9 per cent for loans from official creditors such as governments and multilateral institutions. Private lenders also offered an average repayment period of 12 years, compared with 25 years for official creditors. item.title: 2027: Security tops as APC-PCC unveils 4-point manifesto
item.description: By Soni Daniel, Emma Ujah & Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—The Presidency yesterday asked Nigerians to study the past and current manifestoes of the All Progressives Congress, APC, and judge the party by the promises it has kept since 2023 when it assumed power. Read Also: Security of lives and property to top Tinubu’s agenda in 2nd term – APC The Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, also said President Bola Tinubu will pay priority attention to protection of lives and property if he wins the presidential election on January 16, 2027. Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, who made the declaration at the unveiling of the APC manifesto, titled ‘’From Reforms to Prosperity,’’ described the manifesto as a binding pact with the electorate. “A manifesto, in its strictest sense, is simply a contract between the people and their leaders. It is an inviolable contract, and we take the strict interpretation of what a manifesto represents as gospel under this administration,” he said. He admitted that the reforms had put real pressure on households, adding that the people living through it deserve to be heard. “Nobody should have to pretend that life is easy at the moment,” he said. The former House of Representatives’ Speaker, nonetheless, defended President Tinubu’s decision to act, saying the President confronted the subsidy burden and a distorted foreign exchange system when he took responsibility for the country in 2023. He said: “Leaving those problems untouched would have continued to weaken our ability to invest in the future. The difference between a politician and a leader is that while a politician thinks about the next election, a leader thinks about the next generation. And that is exactly what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has demonstrated. Four pillars The manifesto rests on four pillars, including a secure and resilient nation; a better quality and more affordable life for every Nigerian; energy, infrastructure and economic growth; and effective and accountable governance. They are tied to the eight priority areas of the Renewed Hope Agenda, which the document said would be carried out on four foundations – macroeconomic stability; the rule of law; institutional capability; and national cohesion. By 2031, the document commits to power generation scaled towards 10,000 megawatts, annual economic growth of six per cent, and youth unemployment and out-of-school children, both halved. It also promises 20,000 additional teachers and health insurance expanded from more than 23 million enrollees to 40 per cent of Nigerians. Primary health centres will function in at least 90 per cent of facilities, up from the current 53 per cent. It further promises to work towards 200,000 homes under the Tinubu Mass Social Housing Scheme, Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria, FMBN, mortgages and licensed private developers, tracked on a public dashboard. item.title: Tinubu Won 2023 Election On His Own, Buhari Didn’t Fully Support Him – APC’s Hassan
item.description: A spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Alwan Hassan, has said President Bola Tinubu won the 2023 presidential election against all odds, insisting that former President Muhammadu Buhari did not fully support his candidacy. Hassan said Tinubu secured victory largely through his own political strength, arguing that Buhari did not actively stand behind the APC candidate during the build-up to the election. He made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , while discussing the president’s chances of securing re-election in 2027. During the interview, Hassan was asked whether Tinubu would benefit from the organic political structure and support base associated with his predecessor, particularly as the APC prepares for another presidential contest in the next two months. In response, the APC stalwart questioned whether Buhari had given Tinubu the full backing of his political structure in 2023. “Did he enjoy that in 2023? Did we enjoy Buhari’s support in 2023? Let the truth be told, we did not,” he said. ﻿ When asked whether he was suggesting that Tinubu won the 2023 election on his own, Hassan answered in the affirmative, maintaining that the former president did not fully support his successor’s ambition. “On his own. Buhari didn’t fully come out to support Tinubu,” he said. He further argued that Buhari did not actively campaign for Tinubu during the 2023 election, despite both politicians belonging to the same political party. “Buhari didn’t do well in 2023. He didn’t actually come out to stand for us and stand for Asiwaju in 2023. Asiwaju won that election against all odds,” Hassan said. item.title: [VIDEO] Wike’s ₦10m Pledge: INEC, Police Can Trigger Investigation, Says Okoye
item.description: A former National Commissioner of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Festus Okoye, says the commission, the police and other law enforcement agencies can initiate an investigation into the ₦10 million pledge by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to councillors ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okoye, a lawyer, said this on Tuesday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He said the absence of action by INEC would not prevent individuals or other relevant authorities from raising concerns or investigating the matter if an electoral offence was suspected. “If INEC is not taking this up, can anyone petition on this matter to say, I think Minister Wike is doing the wrong thing? Is it possible? Oh, definitely, yes,” he said. ﻿ The ex-commissioner added that the state could also initiate action if an offence had been committed, while law enforcement agencies could investigate where they believed there were grounds to suspect a violation. Mr Okoye said INEC could equally petition the relevant authorities to investigate the matter and prosecute anyone found culpable. Wike had pledged ₦10 million to each FCT councillor who successfully delivers their ward for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 elections. item.description: The Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the Benue State Government of plotting to disrupt the planned visit of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to the state, an allegation the government has dismissed as false. Obi is scheduled to visit Benue State on Wednesday for a town hall meeting in Makurdi and a humanitarian visit to Yelewata, where he is expected to pay tribute to victims of the June 2025 massacre and commiserate with their families. Addressing journalists in Makurdi on Tuesday, the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Terhemba Shija, called on the state government and security agencies to guarantee the safety of Obi and his supporters. Shija alleged that the government had issued threats aimed at preventing the former Anambra State governor from visiting Yelewata, recalling an earlier attempt to stop him from visiting the community. He said the party had notified the state government and security agencies of the planned visit, adding that its arrangements were already in place. “This letter addressed to His Excellency, the Executive Governor of Benue, was received on the 10th of November, which is today. “While we discuss with the security agency, all they require is that we should send them an itinerary of our visit. I’m going to soon embark on the visit of all the local governments. All I have told the DG to do is to write the itinerary, the times that we’ll be here, and then they will follow,” he said, displaying a copy of the correspondence. ﻿ Shija maintained that the party did not require permission from the state government to conduct its political activities but had notified the authorities in the interest of a peaceful visit. He described Obi’s planned trip as both humanitarian and political, saying the presidential candidate would lay a wreath at the cenotaph erected in memory of the victims of the Yelewata massacre along the Lafia Road. The NDC governorship candidate said Obi would also meet relatives of the victims but would not visit any government facility or internally displaced persons’ camp. According to him, the town hall meeting would be held at the multipurpose hall of the Mission House in Makurdi, behind the Benue Links head office in Wurukum. Shija alleged that the state government was unhappy with Obi’s visit because of its potential political implications ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also accused the government of being behind an earlier attempt to disrupt the presidential candidate’s visit to Yelewata, claiming that suspected supporters of the slogan, “No Alia, No Benue”, had mobilised to prevent him from accessing the community. item.title: Makinde Presents ₦1.115tn 2027 Budget To Oyo Assembly
item.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has presented a proposed budget of ₦1.115 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration and approval. Tagged the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, the proposal is valued at ₦1,115,341,378,359.90. Presenting the budget on Tuesday at the Assembly complex in Agodi, Ibadan, Makinde said it was designed to consolidate the gains of his administration and lay a foundation for sustainable development beyond its tenure. He described it as the final budget proposal of his administration, saying it would sustain the state’s development momentum and ensure continuity after the transition to a new government. “As we prepare to hand over the baton to the next administration, we bring before you the 2027 Budget of Sustained Progress. It is designed to consolidate our gains, sustain public services and carry our state’s development forward through the transition period and beyond,” he said. The governor said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, community development and the strengthening of public institutions, with significant allocations for capital projects in health, education and road infrastructure. He added that his administration was committed to leaving behind clear records, properly documented processes and institutions capable of sustaining efficient service delivery. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Makinde said Oyo State’s Internally Generated Revenue increased by 288 per cent, from ₦26.59 billion in 2019 to ₦103.25 billion in 2025. He also noted that the state ranked third nationally in the 2025 Subnational Ease of Doing Business Assessment. The governor said targeted interventions and partnerships had helped return about 65,000 out-of-school children to classrooms, alongside investments in educational infrastructure, recruitment and service delivery. He, however, said the administration’s performance should be measured beyond revenue figures and rankings. “Figures alone cannot fully assess our administration. The real measure of success is the impact we have made on the lives of our people and the institutions we have built to serve them beyond May 29, 2027,” he said. Makinde also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to women’s inclusion in governance, pledging to sustain the 35 per cent affirmative action policy for women. On infrastructure and agriculture, he said the government had prioritised strategic road projects to connect economic corridors, improve market access and create opportunities for farmers, businesses and rural communities. He said the establishment of the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency had helped reposition agriculture as a viable business sector, while the Oyo State Agribusiness Transformation Centre had become a hub for agricultural investment.
